subject: HorizonML late-stage -> GPU slice heatmap fit & provisional commit
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah@horizonml.com>
Cc: HorizonML Procurement <procure@horizonml.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: HZN-412: GPU slice heatmap fit & provisional commit request

Team / Sarah —

HorizonML is in the final procurement loop for the POC + first-year commit (deal HZN-2026-412). They shared workload characteristics this morning (attached). Before we route to Legal/Finance I need an ops-level read on whether we can safely map this workload to our fleet and—if reasonable—place a short provisional soft-hold on capacity.

High-level ask:
- Confirm which clusters/pod slices can satisfy the workload without exceeding thermal headroom for 24/7 3-week runs.
- Recommend a mapping (cluster + node count + preferred SKU e.g., A100 80GB / A100s quantized) and expected steady throughput.
- Estimate how much burst capacity we can guarantee for 8 weeks post-POC (target burst: +50% tokens/sec).
- If fleet constraints exist, propose fallbacks (e.g., mixed A100 + Q8 quantized T4 pool) and the expected perf/cost delta.
- If OK, open an ops provisional soft-hold tagged HZN-412 for 30 days and confirm owner/next steps.

Requirements (from HorizonML):
- Sustained decoding throughput equivalent to ~40 x A100-80GB (80B-parameter model, moderate prompt lengths)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for interactive endpoints
- KV cache lifetimes ~48 hours, cold-starts infrequent

Attachments: horizon_poc_requirements.pdf (customer-provided), hotspot-heatmap-0612.csv (sample heatmap).

Timeline: Procurement requests confirmation by EOD so they can include capacity language in the final SOW.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0162
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah@horizonml.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HZN-412: GPU slice heatmap fit & provisional commit request

Grace / Sarah —

Quick ops read below after an initial slot scan and thermal-affinity check. I pulled cluster inventories and overlaid the attached heatmap. Notes:  

Inventory snapshot (available as of 2026-08-25 09:45 PDT):
- Cluster east-us-1: 56 x A100-80GB usable (thermal bin B), 32 x A100-40GB (bin C)
- Cluster west-us-2: 24 x A100-80GB (bin A, cooler racks), 120 x T4/Q8-quantized nodes
- Occupancy windows: east-us-1 has recurring production windows Mon-Fri 06:00–20:00 (local), west-us-2 has lower utilization evenings/weekends.

Fit recommendation:
- Steady-state: provision 40 A100-80GB from a split across east-us-1 (24) + west-us-2 (16) to reduce thermal concentration; map requests with affinity tags to avoid single-rack hot spots.
- Burst: we can commit +50% burst (up to ~60 A100-equivalents) for an 8-week ramp if we soft-reserve 18 additional A100-equivalents and allow autoscaling across west-us-2 during off-peak hours.  
- Fallback: if A100 pool contention occurs, we can run a hybrid configuration: 30 A100 + 20 Q8-quantized TFLOPs on T4 fleet — expect ~12–18% higher per-token latency and ~22% lower cost-efficiency.

Operational caveats & actions:
1) Thermal margin: west-us-2 racks (bin A) are preferred for burst windows; east-us-1 will need cross-rack placement to avoid overheating a single POD.
2) KV cache: recommend persistent cache on east-us-1 for locality and a short TTL fallback to west-us-2.
3) Provisional soft-hold: ops can create a 30-day provisional allocation tagged HZN-412 in OPS-2345 with a 72-hour SLA to convert it to a formal reserved commit once SOW countersigned. I will open the ticket if you confirm.
4) Telemetry: we will add a per-route token cost/latency probe and include a perf snapshot at T+7 days once the soft-hold is active.

Request: Grace — please confirm we should open OPS-2345 soft-hold for HZN-412. If yes, I will request PodOps to tag nodes and lock scheduling windows.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lee <sarah@horizonml.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HZN-412: GPU slice heatmap fit & provisional commit request

+1 to Marcus' plan — approve opening a 30-day provisional soft-hold (OPS-2345) and tag HZN-412.

Addenda: If we anticipate multinational usage later in H2, request to prequal EU-AZ fallback (quantized) now — saves ~10 days later. If Sarah needs lower cost for POC, offer mixed-mode (A100 lanes for p95-critical routes + quantized T4 for background batch).

—Rishi
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah@horizonml.com>, HorizonML Procurement <procure@horizonml.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HZN-412: GPU slice heatmap fit & provisional commit request

Sarah / Procurement —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Per ops: we will open a 30-day provisional soft-hold (OPS-2345, tag HZN-412) and provision the steady-state mapping across east-us-1 + west-us-2 as described. Marcus will create the soft-hold ticket and attach the initial thermal placement plan; Rishi has approved the move.

Next steps for HorizonML:
- I will share the soft-hold confirmation and the OPS ticket link by EOD and route this language into the SOW (clause: "conditional provisional capacity hold pending countersignature, 30-day window").
- Please provide the final signature timeline. If we have countersignature within the 30-day hold, we will convert to a reserved commit per the deal terms.
- Schedule: propose a 30-minute handoff with Marcus (ops) and your infra lead Thursday 10:30 AM PT to review the thermal map and request routing.

Attachments included for reference: horizon_poc_requirements.pdf, hotspot-heatmap-0612.csv

Grace O'Connor
